solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Clear picture?

definitions.meaning: plain and unambiguous, with no shades of grey
an old monochrome film or photograph, the question mark flagging the loose definition

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether an image is sharp and easy to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the theme: Cilla Black, the Liverpool singer and TV presenter, was born Priscilla White.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stated starkly with no ambiguity is put this way, and pre-colour films and photos were made in these two tones.

clue.text: Brook's Brothers are into farm equipment

indicators.note: are into says the two letters go inside the machine's name

parts.note: a baler is a farm machine that bundles hay or straw
B is the abbreviation for brother, so two brothers give two Bs

explanation.surface: A clothing chain's founders getting into tractors and tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook's Brothers' suggests the clothing firm Brooks Brothers; here 'Brook's' means 'brook is', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is traditionally said to babble, so poetically a stream is a chatterer.

clue.text: 1 across's who should have followed suit?

definitions.text: 1 across's who should have followed suit?

parts.words: 1 across's who should have followed suit?
parts.note: in bridge and similar card games a player holding a card of the suit led must play it, so a player holding hearts had to follow a heart lead

explanation.surface: A card player grumbling about a partner who failed to follow suit.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across's' means Cilla Black's: this was one of her biggest hits, a 1964 number one.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title, read literally, describes any card player holding a heart, who was obliged to play it when hearts were led.

clue.text: Men have understood

parts.note: chess men: K for king and N for knight
to have is to own or possess

explanation.surface: A terse remark that men have grasped something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' means chess pieces, giving the notation letters K (king) and N (knight).
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood is recognised and familiar, a past participle meaning grasped or recognised.

clue.text: No recordings, no sound

parts.note: taken as written
a tape is a recording medium
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A silent studio with nothing being recorded and not a whisper heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recordings' supplies two different formats, TAPE and EP.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes complete silence: nobody made the slightest noise or complaint.

clue.text: Welcome extremely bad pest

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word Welcome

parts.note: evil means wicked, very bad

explanation.surface: A greeting for an extremely unwelcome bug.
explanation.definitionFit: This small beetle damages grain and crops, making it a classic farm and larder nuisance.

clue.text: Sign in designer pet boarding

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and so going into the designer's name

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French fashion designer
a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: A notice in a fashion designer's kennels announcing the pets being boarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge or pointer is a sign showing a state or trend, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Suffer under a measure of junk, maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue under places the illness word below the measure

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of type width
to ail is to be unwell, to suffer

explanation.surface: Someone suffering beneath a pile of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk, maybe' defines by example: spam is unwanted electronic post.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk messages are one kind of electronic post, so the definition gives an example.

clue.text: Make good salesman strain

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a strain is a melody or tune, as is an air

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a salesman good, despite the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests effort or stress; here it is a musical strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good damage is to fix or mend it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Test expert in bar trade

definitions.meaning: Geoffrey ..., the England opening batsman in Test (international) cricket
to refuse to deal with a country or firm

explanation.surface: A trade expert being tested in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket match; Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England opener.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of a celebrated Yorkshire batsman; the other is a refusal to buy or deal with someone.

clue.text: Denouement for checker's mate, perhaps

parts.note: a chess player who checkmates reaches this final phase of the game, the climax of the play

explanation.surface: The final twist in a story about a checker's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checker's mate' suggests a friend of an inspector; it is a chess player delivering checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing phase of a chess game, where checkmate comes, also means the final stage of any process.

clue.text: Sheets maybe a bit small in envelope

indicators.note: a bit of says the answer is a fragment taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Folded sheets, perhaps, a little too big for an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed sheets are an example of household cloth goods, traditionally made from flax fabric.

clue.text: Publicity is all leading back to 1 across

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
taken as written

indicators.note: back says the words all and leading are read in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written
IC is in charge, so leading

explanation.surface: Publicity that brings everything back to a black-and-white picture.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' is the theme: Cilla Black was born Priscilla White, and her full first name 'leads' to White.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the full forename of the theme singer, whose birth name ended in the colour White.

clue.text: With warm rub, athlete's foot turned pale brown

indicators.note: turned means the letters are churned into a new order
foot means the bottom, the last letter, of the word athlete

explanation.surface: Treating athlete's foot with a warm rub until it changes colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' shuffles WARM RUB with E, the foot of 'athlete'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an earth pigment used by painters, giving a light yellowish-brown colour before roasting darkens it.

clue.text: Confuse maids with a lot of milk producers

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: relating to nipple-shaped parts

indicators.note: confuse means mix up the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Mixing up dairymaids with a large herd of cows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk producers' suggests cows; here it means nipples, from the Greek for breast-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The word derives from the Greek mastos, a breast, and describes something shaped like a teat.

clue.text: Cutter sailing boat The Queen loses bow

indicators.note: the bow is the front, so the boat's word drops its first letter

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A cutter, the sailing boat, damaged at the bow while the Queen is aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like the sailing vessel; it is someone who cuts designs.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver cuts lines into metal plates with acid or a needle, so is literally a cutter.

clue.text: See 2
While Eliot dreams

parts.note: while in the sense of although
T. S. Eliot, the poet

explanation.surface: A poet daydreaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreams are ideas in the mind, a plural noun for imaginings or musings.

clue.text: 1 across's tongue stew

definitions.meaning: Cilla Black was from Liverpool, whose dialect bears this name
a Liverpool dish of meat, potatoes and onions

explanation.surface: A singer's tongue cooked in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a Liverpudlian; Liverpool's accent and its traditional lamb or beef stew share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Liverpool dialect and the sailors' meat stew from which Liverpudlians got their nickname.

clue.text: Stealthily avoid Spooner's spot of light breathing

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a blip is a spot of light on a radar screen
a sigh is a deep audible breath

explanation.surface: Slipping past unnoticed while breathing lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass unnoticed or evade quietly is the phrasal verb's sense, as time does when it passes.

clue.text: Rivals playwright forger for 1 across player

parts.note: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote the comedy The Rivals
a blacksmith forges iron

explanation.surface: A rival playwright forging a classic drama for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' suggests a counterfeiter; it is a blacksmith at the forge.
explanation.definitionFit: This actress played Cilla Black in the 2014 ITV drama Cilla, so she is the theme's player.

clue.text: Warn eye make-up will require change at end of date

definitions.text: will require change at end of date
definitions.note: a noun phrase: the occasion when the year at the end of a written date must change

indicators.note: make-up means the letters are made up afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that eye make-up needs changing by the end of a date.
explanation.walkthrough: In day-month-year dates the year comes last, so the first of January means writing a new last part.
explanation.definitionFit: On the first of January the year number written at the end of a date goes up by one.

clue.text: Former characters from Whitby go needy

indicators.note: characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Former residents of a Yorkshire seaside town falling on hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from times past is earlier or previous, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: 1 across's from one passing receiver

parts.note: this is what someone says on handing a telephone handset to another person, and also a Cilla Black song

explanation.surface: A singer's song heard from someone passing a radio receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' means a telephone handset; '1 across's' marks a Cilla Black hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is spoken when handing over the phone, and is the title of a 1964 Lennon-McCartney song recorded by Cilla.

clue.text: See 19
Present contains surprise? Emphatically not!

indicators.note: contains says the time word wraps round the exclamation

parts.note: the present moment is now
oh is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Asked whether a present holds a surprise, someone flatly denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift; it is the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect adverb means in no way at all, a forceful refusal.

clue.text: Fool about with explosive material

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An idiot fooling about with explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a main ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Prevent from seeing chocolate Derek has hidden

indicators.note: has hidden says the actress's name surrounds the chocolate

parts.note: Bo Derek, the actress of the film 10
Lindt is a Swiss chocolate brand

explanation.surface: Someone named Derek hiding his chocolate so nobody sees it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derek' looks like a first name; it is a surname, the actress Bo Derek's. Strictly the phrase means unable to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made unaware of something is to be kept from perceiving it, as in being blinded to its faults.

clue.text: Appointment one expects to lead to congress

definitions.text: Appointment one expects to lead to congress

parts.words: Appointment one expects to lead to congress
parts.note: congress here means sexual intercourse, so this is a romantic engagement with high hopes

explanation.surface: A meeting that should lead to a political assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congress' suggests a legislature; it is used in its old sense of sexual union.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate romantic engagement is one where the evening is expected to end in bed.

clue.text: Hurriedly gutted teal overwhelmed by smells returning after high water

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the high water

parts.note: Elter Water is a small lake in the English Lake District

indicators.note: returning means the whole bundle is read backwards
overwhelmed by says the gutted bird goes inside the word for smells

parts.note: reeks means smells strongly

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of the word teal are removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A teal hurriedly gutted, its stink lingering after a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high water' looks like a flood, but it is two pieces: H for high and a small Lake District lake. 'returning' turns RETLEKS round to make SKELTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The reduplicated adverb means in disorderly haste, rushing in confusion.
